`Picard/JacobianDataCharts.lean` and un-rooted it from `AlgebraicJacobian.lean` in one commit).

The mechanism is not a bug in anyone's lane, it is the direct consequence of §1: a CAS commit
publishes a tree built in a **private** `GIT_INDEX_FILE` and moves the ref with `update-ref`.
The **shared** index is never touched, so the moment anybody commits, the shared index still
describes the previous HEAD — and `git status` then reports that difference as *staged changes*,
including **staged deletions** for any file the commit added. The longer a run goes, the further
the shared index drifts behind.

Consequences, all three binding:

1. **Never run a bare `git commit` (no `-a`, no pathspec) against `workspace.git`.** It publishes
   whatever the stale shared index holds, which is a reversion of other lanes' work.
2. **Before finishing, check and repair.** `git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. status --porcelain | grep '^D'`
   must be empty. If it is not, repair with the **narrowest** form that covers your paths:
   `git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. reset -q -- <your project dir>/`. Prefer this to a whole-index
   `read-tree HEAD` when another run is live — a full reset can discard the other run's staging.
3. **Verify the worktree is the good copy before repairing.** `reset` makes the index match HEAD;
   that is only safe once you have confirmed the on-disk file is the one you want
   (`diff <(git --git-dir=$GD cat-file -p HEAD:<path>) <path>`).

Expect to repeat step 2 more than once in a long session: every CAS commit by any lane re-stales
the index, so a repair done early does not stay done.

## 2. The lake mutex is a mkdir DIRECTORY lock — never flock a file there

`/tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock` is acquired by `mkdir` (atomic; a crash leaves a
directory that the next holder's timeout logic can reap). It is NOT a flock file: a lane
that runs `flock /tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock …` creates a plain FILE at the
path, and every mkdir-acquire loop then spins forever (this deadlocked all lanes
15:18–19:10 on 2026-07-16 until a human deleted it). Acquire pattern:

```bash
LOCK=/tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock
while ! mkdir "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null; do
  # (a) plain FILE at the path = a flock protocol-violation; reap immediately.
  if [ -f "$LOCK" ]; then echo "STALE: plain file at $LOCK (flock violation) — removing" >&2; rm -f "$LOCK"; continue; fi
  # (b) orphaned DIRECTORY from a crashed build (rmdir never ran). Reap on proof of death:
  if [ -d "$LOCK" ]; then
    holder=$(cat "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null)
    if [ -n "$holder" ] && ! kill -0 "$holder" 2>/dev/null; then
      echo "STALE: holder pid $holder dead — reaping" >&2; rm -rf "$LOCK"; continue
    fi
    # No pidfile (old-cohort holder): reap only if NO live lake build AND the dir is >15 min old.
    if [ -z "$holder" ] && ! pgrep -f 'lake build AlgebraicJacobian' >/dev/null 2>&1 \
       && [ $(( $(date +%s) - $(stat -c %Y "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null || date +%s) )) -gt 900 ]; then
      echo "STALE: no live build, lock >15min old — reaping" >&2; rm -rf "$LOCK"; continue
    fi
  fi
  sleep 10
done
echo $$ > "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null      # record holder so a later reaper can prove liveness via kill -0
# … lake build … ; rm -rf "$LOCK"      # release (rm -rf, not rmdir — the pidfile makes the dir non-empty)
```

### 2a. THE RELEASE IS AS DANGEROUS AS THE REAP — check the pidfile before `rm -rf` (2026-07-28, run 0072)

The acquire loop above is careful; the release (`rm -rf "$LOCK"`) is not, and that asymmetry
caused a real incident. **A lane removed the lock directory while its pidfile named a LIVE pid
belonging to another lane's build**, having printed `ALIVE` for that pid one line earlier.

The mechanism is worth stating because nothing in the recipe warns about it. The offending lane
had legitimately acquired the lock, and then **its own shell was killed by a harness timeout
while it held it**. On the next turn it reasoned "the lock is mine and my holder is dead, so
release it" — but in the interval a *different* lane had acquired the lock, so the pid in the
file had never been its own. The lane was running the release branch on a belief about history
rather than on a reading of the file.

> **Before `rm -rf "$LOCK"`, verify the pidfile still names YOUR pid.**
> `[ "$(cat "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null)" = "$$" ] && rm -rf "$LOCK"`
> If it names anything else, the lock is not yours to release: say so and leave it alone.

Two corollaries:

* **"It was mine a minute ago" is not evidence**, especially when a harness can kill the shell
  between acquire and release. Every turn boundary is a window for another lane to take the lock.
* **Do not "repair" the mistake by re-creating the directory with the other lane's pid.**
  Fabricating a pidfile for a build you do not own makes the lock unreapable by its real owner
  and hides the incident. Report it on the thread and let the owner re-take it.

For long builds, prefer a form that cannot outlive its own hold: run the build detached with a
### 4a. A MINUS line in that diff is never yours (2026-07-28, run 0072)

The check above works. The failure mode is **misreading** it, and it happened again on
2026-07-28: the diff printed a `-import`/`+import` pair from a sibling lane's *uncommitted*
worktree edit, the committing lane read it as background noise, and the commit published the
sibling's replacement — dropping `Picard/DivRepAffPullIndep.lean` from the import closure.
The file stayed in HEAD and still compiled, but was reachable from nothing: **un-rooted**,
i.e. I-0153 again, from a lane that had run the I-0153 check.

So state the rule in a form that needs no judgement:

> **A `-import` line in that diff is never yours.** The only clean result is `+import <your
> file>` and nothing else. Any minus line means you are about to delete another lane's root
> entry — stop and explain it before committing. An unexplained `+import` you did not write
> is the same signal: a sibling's uncommitted edit is in your worktree copy, and a minus line
> usually accompanies it.

This is strictly stronger than "commit only your own lines", because you can intend that and
still sweep — staging the whole file is what publishes their edit, and the diff is your only
warning.

**Repair additively, never by reverting.** Restore the dropped import while **keeping** the
other lane's new one, then verify with a full root build (the 2026-07-28 repair: 9139 jobs,
exit 0, with the un-rooted file rebuilt). Reverting to your own earlier root blob discards
their work and turns one incident into two.

## 5. The AJCR mutex is for AJCR lake invocations only

No cross-workspace use (an OpenGA-Horizon agent squatted it ~25 min for its own
`lake cache get`, silently serializing AJCR lanes against unrelated work). Other
workspaces must use their own lock paths.

### 5a. Read it as per-PROJECT, not per-workspace (2026-07-28, run 0072)

The rule above says "cross-workspace", and that wording has a hole: **AJC and AJCR are two
projects in the SAME workspace.** Observed live on 2026-07-28 — the AJCR mutex was held for
over ten minutes while the only live `lake build` belonged to an `ajc-*` lane building
`MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge`, the sibling project. Same failure as the
OpenGA incident, not covered by the rule as written.

The lock path is `ajcr-locks`, so read the rule as: **only lanes building
`Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild` may take it.** AJC lanes need their own path
(`/tmp/claude-1001/ajc-locks/lake.lock`). Note the AJC task prompts do not mention a mutex
at all, which is very likely why an AJC lane reached for this one.

### 5b. Write the pidfile — the no-pidfile fallback cannot distinguish squatter from orphan

§2's acquire recipe writes `$$` into `$LOCK/pid` so a later lane can prove death via
`kill -0`. In the incident above the lock directory had **no pidfile**, so that branch could
not fire and the fallback ("no live `lake build AlgebraicJacobian` **and** dir >15 min old")
also could not fire — there *was* a live build, just not an AJCR one. Net effect: a
provably-non-AJCR holder is unreapable for 15 minutes.

Two consequences for a blocked lane, both applied in that incident:

* **Do not reap a directory whose holder you cannot prove dead**, even when you suspect a
  squatter. Reaping mid-build is worse than waiting.
* **Fall back to the narrowest check instead of blocking.** `lake env lean <file>` on the
  single changed file writes no shared build state and needs no lock; it is a faithful
  kernel check for that file. Record in the report that the mutex was unavailable and which
  check you substituted.

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivRepAwaySpanGlue

/-!
# Pushing an away cover forward along an algebra map

The `pull_naturality` field of `DivRepAffinePullback` compares the forward map at `A` with
the forward map at `B` along a `k`-algebra map `φ : A →ₐ[k] B`.  The forward map is built
from an atlas factorization over a spanning family `f : Fin m → A`, so naturality needs the
*pushed* family `φ ∘ f : Fin m → B` and the induced comparison of carriers.

This file supplies that transport, at the canonical carriers, over `k`:

* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivFamZar.awayPush` — the induced `k`-algebra map
  `Localization.Away a →ₐ[k] Localization.Away (φ a)`, i.e. mathlib's
  `Localization.awayMap` upgraded over the base field.  Characterized by
  `awayPush_algebraMap`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivFamZar.awayPush_comp_toAlgHom` — the square with the two structure
  maps: pushing forward after restricting to `Localization.Away a` is restricting to
  `Localization.Away (φ a)` after `φ`.  This is the identity that turns naturality of the
  forward map into a statement about the pushed cover.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivFamZar.span_range_map_eq_top` — the pushed family still spans, so
  it is again an admissible cover.

Nothing here mentions divisors: it is the localization bookkeeping the naturality field
needs, isolated so that the naturality proof itself reads as a comparison of glued values.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

namespace DivFamZar

variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
variable {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]

/-! ## The pushed carrier

**This is mathlib's map, not ours.**  `Localization.awayMapₐ`
(`Mathlib/RingTheory/Localization/Away/Basic.lean`) already gives
`Localization.Away a →ₐ[R] Localization.Away (f a)` for `f : A →ₐ[R] B` over an arbitrary
base ring `R`, which is exactly the transport this lane needs at `R := k`.  An earlier draft
of this file re-derived it from the `RingHom`-level `Localization.awayMap` by supplying
`commutes'` by hand; a fresh-context review caught the duplication.  What remains here is the
naturality square, which mathlib does not state in the `IsScalarTower.toAlgHom` spelling the
`DivFamZar` statements use. -/

/-- **The characterizing property of the pushed carrier map**: on the image of `A`,
`Localization.awayMapₐ φ a` is `φ` followed by the structure map of the pushed carrier. -/
@[simp]
theorem awayMapₐ_algebraMap (φ : A →ₐ[k] B) (a : A) (x : A) :
    Localization.awayMapₐ φ a (algebraMap A (Localization.Away a) x)
      = algebraMap B (Localization.Away (φ a)) (φ x) := by
  simp [Localization.awayMapₐ, IsLocalization.Away.mapₐ, IsLocalization.Away.map]

/-- **The naturality square of the away carriers**: restricting to `Localization.Away a` and
then pushing forward along `φ` is the same as applying `φ` and then restricting to
`Localization.Away (φ a)`.  This is the identity that converts `pull_naturality` into a
comparison over the pushed cover, and it is the one thing here that mathlib does not already
state — its `awayMapₐ` lemmas are in the `algebraMap A (Localization.Away a)` spelling, while
the `DivFamZar.mapAlgHom` statements consume `IsScalarTower.toAlgHom`. -/
theorem awayMapₐ_comp_toAlgHom (φ : A →ₐ[k] B) (a : A) :
    (Localization.awayMapₐ φ a).comp (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k A (Localization.Away a))
      = (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k B (Localization.Away (φ a))).comp φ :=
  AlgHom.ext fun x => awayMapₐ_algebraMap φ a x

/-! ## The pushed cover is a cover -/

/-- **The pushed family still spans**: the image of a spanning family under a ring
homomorphism spans the unit ideal of the target, so an away cover pushes forward to an away
cover. -/
theorem span_range_map_eq_top {ι : Type} (φ : A →ₐ[k] B) (f : ι → A)
    (hspan : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤) :
    Ideal.span (Set.range fun t => φ (f t)) = ⊤ := by
  have himg : Ideal.map φ.toRingHom (Ideal.span (Set.range f))
      = Ideal.span (Set.range fun t => φ (f t)) := by
    rw [Ideal.map_span, ← Set.range_comp]
    rfl
  rw [← himg, hspan, Ideal.map_top]

end DivFamZar

end AlgebraicGeometry

    11	# Descent of the admissible away-local divisor family
    12	
    13	The Noetherian spreading theorem applies after descending a cocycle datum to a finitely

    15	where they form an etale algebra carrying the same widened divisor family.

    69	/-- An admissible fibre of a cocycle datum over an arbitrary affine base lifts to a widened
    70	divisor family after an etale base change, with a chosen prime above the input prime. -/
    71	theorem exists_etale_divFamZarAff_of_admissible_fibre
    72	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
    73	    (hpi : pi ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) (n g : ℕ)
    74	    (hchi : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
    75	    (hgn : g ≤ n)
    76	    (hdeg : ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] [Algebra B K]
    77	      [IsScalarTower k B K],
    78	      classDeg K (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B K) D.cechPicClass) =
    79	        (n : ℤ))
    80	    (p : PrimeSpectrum B)
    81	    (hp : D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
    82	    ∃ (S : Type u) (_ : CommRing S) (_ : Algebra k S) (_ : Algebra B S)

    84	      (q : PrimeSpectrum S),
    85	      PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap B S) q = p ∧
    86	        ∃ F : DivFamZarAff C S n,
    87	          F.picClass = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B S) D.cechPicClass := by
    88	  obtain ⟨B₀, -, hnoeth, D₀, hbc⟩ := D.exists_fg_isNoetherianRing_baseChange_eq
    89	  letI : IsNoetherianRing (↑B₀) := hnoeth
    90	  let phi : (↑B₀) →ₐ[k] B := IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k (↑B₀) B
    91	  let p₀ : PrimeSpectrum (↑B₀) :=
    92	    PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap (↑B₀) B) p
    93	  have hcom : p₀.asIdeal = p.asIdeal.comap (algebraMap (↑B₀) B) := rfl
    94	  let rho : p₀.asIdeal.ResidueField →ₐ[k] p.asIdeal.ResidueField :=
    95	    Ideal.ResidueField.mapₐ p₀.asIdeal p.asIdeal phi hcom
    96	  letI : Algebra p₀.asIdeal.ResidueField p.asIdeal.ResidueField :=
    97	    rho.toRingHom.toAlgebra
    98	  haveI : IsScalarTower k p₀.asIdeal.ResidueField p.asIdeal.ResidueField :=
    99	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun x => (rho.commutes x).symm
   100	  haveI : IsScalarTower (↑B₀) p₀.asIdeal.ResidueField
   101	      p.asIdeal.ResidueField :=
   102	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun x => by
   103	      change algebraMap (↑B₀) p.asIdeal.ResidueField x =
   104	        rho (algebraMap (↑B₀) p₀.asIdeal.ResidueField x)
   105	      rw [Ideal.ResidueField.mapₐ_apply, Ideal.ResidueField.map_algebraMap]
   106	      exact IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply (↑B₀) B p.asIdeal.ResidueField x
   107	  have hclp : Scheme.CechPic.map
   108	      (relCurveMap C (↑B₀) p.asIdeal.ResidueField) D₀.cechPicClass =
   109	      Scheme.CechPic.map
   110	        (relCurveMap C B p.asIdeal.ResidueField) D.cechPicClass := by
   111	    rw [descent_cechPicClass (C := C) (B := B) hbc,
   112	      ← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp, relCurveMap_comp]
   113	  have hpD₀ : D₀.HasWitnessH1Vanishing p.asIdeal.ResidueField :=
   114	    (D₀.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_congr_of_cechPicClass_eq
   115	      D p.asIdeal.ResidueField hclp).mpr hp
   116	  have hp₀ : D₀.HasWitnessH1Vanishing p₀.asIdeal.ResidueField :=
   117	    (D₀.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension
   118	      p₀.asIdeal.ResidueField p.asIdeal.ResidueField).mpr hpD₀
   119	  have hcurve : (C ◁ Over.overSpecMap rho).left =
   120	      relCurveMap C p₀.asIdeal.ResidueField p.asIdeal.ResidueField := by
   121	    refine congrArg
   122	      (fun t : overSpec k p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⟶
   123	        overSpec k p₀.asIdeal.ResidueField => (C ◁ t).left) ?_
   124	    exact Over.OverMorphism.ext rfl
   125	  have hclass : Scheme.CechPic.map
   126	      (relCurveMap C p₀.asIdeal.ResidueField p.asIdeal.ResidueField)
   127	        (Scheme.CechPic.map
   128	          (relCurveMap C (↑B₀) p₀.asIdeal.ResidueField)
   129	          D₀.cechPicClass) =
   130	      Scheme.CechPic.map
   131	        (relCurveMap C B p.asIdeal.ResidueField) D.cechPicClass := by
   132	    rw [descent_cechPicClass (C := C) (B := B) hbc,
   133	      ← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp, relCurveMap_comp,
   134	      ← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp, relCurveMap_comp]
   135	  have hinv := classDeg_cechPicMap_baseFieldTransition C rho
   136	    (Scheme.CechPic.map
   137	      (relCurveMap C (↑B₀) p₀.asIdeal.ResidueField) D₀.cechPicClass)
   138	  rw [hcurve] at hinv
   139	  have hdeg₀ : classDeg p₀.asIdeal.ResidueField
   140	      (Scheme.CechPic.map
   141	        (relCurveMap C (↑B₀) p₀.asIdeal.ResidueField)
   142	        D₀.cechPicClass) = (n : ℤ) := by
   143	    calc
   144	      _ = classDeg p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   145	          (Scheme.CechPic.map
   146	            (relCurveMap C p₀.asIdeal.ResidueField p.asIdeal.ResidueField)
   147	            (Scheme.CechPic.map
   148	              (relCurveMap C (↑B₀) p₀.asIdeal.ResidueField)
   149	              D₀.cechPicClass)) := hinv.symm
   150	      _ = classDeg p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   151	          (Scheme.CechPic.map
   152	            (relCurveMap C B p.asIdeal.ResidueField) D.cechPicClass) := by
   153	        rw [hclass]
   154	      _ = (n : ℤ) := hdeg p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   155	  obtain ⟨h, hh, q₁, hq₁, f, hf, q₂, hq₂, F₀, hF₀⟩ :=
   156	    D₀.exists_away_away_divFamZarAff_of_admissible_fibre
   157	      hpi n g hchi hgn p₀ hp₀ hdeg₀
   158	  let B₁ := Localization.Away (phi h)
   159	  let phi₁ : Localization.Away h →ₐ[k] B₁ := Localization.awayMapₐ phi h

   161	  let phi₂ : Localization.Away f →ₐ[k] S := Localization.awayMapₐ phi₁ f

   163	    ((algebraMap B₁ S).comp (algebraMap B B₁)).toAlgebra
   164	  letI : Algebra B S := algBS
   165	  letI : SMul B S := algBS.toSMul
   166	  haveI towerBB₁S : IsScalarTower B B₁ S :=
   167	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' rfl
   168	  haveI towerkBS : IsScalarTower k B S :=
   169	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' (by
   170	      rw [RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra, RingHom.comp_assoc,
   171	        ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq k B B₁,
   172	        ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq k B₁ S])
   173	  letI : Algebra.Etale B B₁ := Algebra.Etale.of_isLocalizationAway (phi h)
   174	  letI : Algebra.Etale B₁ S := Algebra.Etale.of_isLocalizationAway (phi₁ f)

   176	  have hph : phi h ∉ p.asIdeal := by
   177	    intro hmem
   178	    apply hh
   179	    exact hmem
   180	  obtain ⟨q₁B, hq₁B⟩ : p ∈ Set.range
   181	      (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap B B₁)) := by
   182	    rw [PrimeSpectrum.localization_away_comap_range B₁ (phi h)]
   183	    exact hph
   184	  have hq₁push : PrimeSpectrum.comap phi₁.toRingHom q₁B = q₁ := by
   185	    apply PrimeSpectrum.localization_comap_injective
   186	      (Localization.Away h) (Submonoid.powers h)
   187	    have hsquare : phi₁.toRingHom.comp
   188	        (algebraMap (↑B₀) (Localization.Away h)) =
   189	        (algebraMap B B₁).comp (algebraMap (↑B₀) B) := by
   190	      ext x
   191	      exact DivFamZar.awayMapₐ_algebraMap phi h x
   192	    calc
   193	      PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap (↑B₀) (Localization.Away h))
   194	          (PrimeSpectrum.comap phi₁.toRingHom q₁B) =
   195	          PrimeSpectrum.comap
   196	            (phi₁.toRingHom.comp
   197	              (algebraMap (↑B₀) (Localization.Away h))) q₁B :=
   198	        (congrFun (PrimeSpectrum.comap_comp
   199	          (algebraMap (↑B₀) (Localization.Away h)) phi₁.toRingHom) q₁B).symm
   200	      _ = PrimeSpectrum.comap
   201	          ((algebraMap B B₁).comp (algebraMap (↑B₀) B)) q₁B := by
   202	        rw [hsquare]
   203	      _ = PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap (↑B₀) B)
   204	          (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap B B₁) q₁B) :=
   205	        congrFun (PrimeSpectrum.comap_comp
   206	          (algebraMap (↑B₀) B) (algebraMap B B₁)) q₁B
   207	      _ = p₀ := by rw [hq₁B]
   208	      _ = PrimeSpectrum.comap
   209	          (algebraMap (↑B₀) (Localization.Away h)) q₁ := hq₁.symm
   210	  have hfB : phi₁ f ∉ q₁B.asIdeal := by
   211	    intro hmem
   212	    apply hf
   213	    have : f ∈ (PrimeSpectrum.comap phi₁.toRingHom q₁B).asIdeal := hmem
   214	    rwa [hq₁push] at this
   215	  obtain ⟨q, hq⟩ : q₁B ∈ Set.range
   216	      (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap B₁ S)) := by
   217	    rw [PrimeSpectrum.localization_away_comap_range S (phi₁ f)]

   219	  have hqB : PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap B S) q = p := by
   220	    rw [IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq B B₁ S, PrimeSpectrum.comap_comp]
   221	    change PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap B B₁)
   222	      (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap B₁ S) q) = p
   223	    rw [hq, hq₁B]
   224	  let algA₂S : Algebra (Localization.Away f) S := phi₂.toRingHom.toAlgebra
   225	  letI : Algebra (Localization.Away f) S := algA₂S
   226	  letI : SMul (Localization.Away f) S := algA₂S.toSMul

   233	  letI : SMul (↑B₀) S := algB₀S.toSMul

   240	    intro x

   257	      (relCurveMap C (Localization.Away f) S) F₀.picClass from

     8	import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Sites.LocallyBijective
     9	import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Sites.RegularEpi
    10	
    11	/-!
    12	# The admissible Abel map after big-etale sheafification
    13	
    14	The big etale site of `Scheme.{u}` requires type-valued sheafification in `Type (u + 1)`.
    15	This module therefore applies `ULift` to the concrete admissible Abel transformation before
    16	sheafifying it. Subcanonicity identifies the sheafified source with the actual representable
    17	Yoneda sheaf of `divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C`.
    18	
    19	The target here is deliberately the etale sheafification of `pic0SigmaFunctor C`; identifying
    20	it with the original Picard functor is a separate mathematical step. The categorical image
    21	of the Abel map is the effective quotient of its kernel pair in the category of etale sheaves.
    22	No Scheme representability conclusion is asserted in this module.
    23	-/
    24	
    25	set_option autoImplicit false
    26	
    27	universe u v w w'
    28	
    29	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
    30	
    31	namespace CategoryTheory.Presheaf
    32	
    33	variable {X : Type u} [Category.{v} X] (J : GrothendieckTopology X)
    34	
    35	/-- Local surjectivity of a type-valued presheaf map survives a universe lift. -/
    36	theorem isLocallySurjective_whiskerRight_ulift
    37	    {F G : Xᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w} (f : F ⟶ G)
    38	    [IsLocallySurjective J f] :
    39	    IsLocallySurjective J
    40	      (Functor.whiskerRight f uliftFunctor.{w', w}) := by
    41	  constructor
    42	  intro U s
    43	  apply J.superset_covering _ (imageSieve_mem J f s.down)
    44	  intro V i hi
    45	  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := hi
    46	  refine ⟨ULift.up t, ?_⟩
    47	  apply ULift.ext
    48	  exact ht
    49	
    50	end CategoryTheory.Presheaf
    51	
    52	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    53	
    54	/-! ## Subcanonicity of the big etale site -/
    55	
    56	/-- The big etale topology on schemes is subcanonical. -/
    57	instance Scheme.subcanonical_etaleTopology : Scheme.etaleTopology.{u}.Subcanonical :=
    58	  GrothendieckTopology.Subcanonical.of_le Scheme.etaleTopology_le_proetaleTopology
    59	
    60	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    61	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    62	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    63	
    64	/-! ## The sheafified concrete Abel map -/
    65	
    66	/-- The big-etale sheafification of the universe-raised Picard Sigma presheaf. -/
    67	noncomputable abbrev pic0SigmaEtaleSheafification :
    68	    Sheaf Scheme.etaleTopology.{u} (Type (u + 1)) :=
    69	  (presheafToSheaf Scheme.etaleTopology (Type (u + 1))).obj
    70	    (pic0SigmaFunctor C ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1})
    71	
    72	/-- Subcanonicity identifies the universe-raised Yoneda sheaf of the admissible divisor
    73	representer with the sheafification of its underlying representable presheaf. -/
    74	noncomputable def admissibleAbelEtaleSourceIso :
    75	    Scheme.etaleTopology.uliftYoneda.{u + 1}.obj
    76	        (divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C).left ≅
    77	      (presheafToSheaf Scheme.etaleTopology (Type (u + 1))).obj
    78	        (yoneda.obj (divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C).left ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1}) :=
    79	  (asIso ((sheafificationAdjunction Scheme.etaleTopology (Type (u + 1))).counit.app
    80	    (Scheme.etaleTopology.uliftYoneda.{u + 1}.obj
    81	      (divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C).left))).symm
    82	
    83	/-- The concrete admissible Abel transformation as a morphism from its representable
    84	big-etale Yoneda source to the sheafification of the Picard Sigma presheaf. -/
    85	noncomputable def admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap :
    86	    Scheme.etaleTopology.uliftYoneda.{u + 1}.obj
    87	        (divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C).left ⟶
    88	      pic0SigmaEtaleSheafification C :=
    89	  (admissibleAbelEtaleSourceIso C).hom ≫
    90	    (presheafToSheaf Scheme.etaleTopology (Type (u + 1))).map
    91	      (Functor.whiskerRight (abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible C) uliftFunctor.{u + 1})
    92	
    93	/-! ## The effective image quotient in etale sheaves -/
    94	
    95	/-- The image sheaf of the concrete admissible Abel map. -/
    96	noncomputable abbrev admissibleAbelEtaleImage :
    97	    Sheaf Scheme.etaleTopology.{u} (Type (u + 1)) :=
    98	  Sheaf.image (admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap C)
    99	
   100	/-- The canonical epimorphism from the admissible divisor source to the Abel image sheaf. -/
   101	noncomputable abbrev admissibleAbelEtaleToImage :
   102	    Scheme.etaleTopology.uliftYoneda.{u + 1}.obj
   103	        (divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C).left ⟶
   104	      admissibleAbelEtaleImage C :=
   105	  Sheaf.toImage (admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap C)
   106	
   107	/-- The kernel pair of the map onto the Abel image is the pullback kernel pair of the original
   108	concrete Abel sheaf map. -/
   109	noncomputable def admissibleAbelEtaleImageKernelPair :
   110	    IsKernelPair (admissibleAbelEtaleToImage C)
   111	      (pullback.fst (admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap C)
   112	        (admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap C))
   113	      (pullback.snd (admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap C)
   114	        (admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap C)) := by
   115	  have hbig : IsKernelPair
   116	      (admissibleAbelEtaleToImage C ≫
   117	        Sheaf.imageι (admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap C))
   118	      (pullback.fst (admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap C)
   119	        (admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap C))
   120	      (pullback.snd (admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap C)
   121	        (admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap C)) := by
   122	    rw [Sheaf.toImage_ι]
   123	    exact IsKernelPair.of_hasPullback (admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap C)
   124	  exact hbig.cancel_right_of_mono
   125	
   126	/-- The Abel image sheaf is the effective coequalizer of the original concrete Abel kernel
   127	pair. This is the sheaf-level quotient; representability of the relation and quotient by
   128	schemes is a separate step. -/
   129	noncomputable def admissibleAbelEtaleImageCoequalizer :
   130	    IsColimit (Cofork.ofπ (admissibleAbelEtaleToImage C)
   131	      (admissibleAbelEtaleImageKernelPair C).w) := by
   132	  haveI : IsRegularEpi (admissibleAbelEtaleToImage C) :=
   133	    IsRegularEpiCategory.regularEpiOfEpi _
   134	  exact (admissibleAbelEtaleImageKernelPair C).toCoequalizer'
